A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IAPO research. All 49 pages of v1 and 45 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, experimental figures, proofs, and extensive appendix case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical and commonsense reasoning experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, inference-time measurements, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses, with revised mathematical benchmark results and training curves.

M1.justification: The three-component token advantage, conditional-MI estimator, KV-cache preloading, and chunk-wise forwarding remain unchanged. Appendix C.1's practical entropy substitution is already disclosed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH-500, DAPO-Math-17k, and CommonsenseQA. The human comparison and reasoning case studies also remain; no new dataset, domain, or task scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain DAPO, GFPO, GTPO, and S-GRPO, with the same base-model comparisons in Table 1. No baseline method is added or replaced.

E3.justification: Table 1 drops the stated rule withholding R@k when corresponding Pass@k underperforms the base model, changing the reported accuracy gate for efficiency comparisons. Dataset splits, model sizes, training budgets, and metric definitions otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix C.4's expanded ablations, including the 1.5B and 7B comparisons, and C.5's multi-setting alpha/beta sensitivity study. The main 0.5B ablation and sensitivity plots are revised, as are training dynamics. Case studies and token heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report plus/minus values and graphical uncertainty bands without specifying run counts, seeds, or confidence levels. Revised uncertainty magnitudes accompany changed results; no new statistical reporting procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3–5 and Figures 5–6 and 9–11 substantially revise results. For IAPO/Qwen2.5-7B on GSM8K, reported P@32 changes from 1.0000 to 0.9805 and L@32 from 111.83 to 83.97; on DAPO-Math-17k they change from 0.6889 to 0.4267 and 194.50 to 429.62. These are revised reported outcomes, not evidence of an improved method. CommonsenseQA and inference-time results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The covariance theorem, length-reduction corollary, exploration argument, and Appendix B derivations retain their substance. Replacing 'keyword' with 'informative' terminology and changing mathematical typesetting do not introduce new assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the maximum token-reduction claim from 36% to 47%, and the introduction specifies a 43% improvement over the best baseline. The underlying contributions remain unchanged; the conclusion still states 36%.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement interprets token savings as sustainability and accessibility benefits and suggests applications beyond language reasoning. Removing Appendix C.5 also removes its assertion that sensitivity conclusions generalize across model–dataset settings. Most mechanism explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, software configuration, and code-access information are retained. However, v2 C.4 deletes v1 C.6's explicit identification of Table 6 samples as Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct outputs on GSM8K, slightly reducing experimental provenance.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the same research positioning. Bibliographic changes update publication metadata and remove the older RLAIF entry while retaining its corresponding 2024 publication; they do not introduce distinct prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and terminology edits, updates author/publication details, and adds conflict-of-interest, acknowledgements, and impact text. Appendix subsections are removed and renumbered, but the main narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The complete supplementary ablation and sensitivity figure sets are removed. Figures 5–6 and 9–11 are redrawn with revised axes, ranges, or labels, and some tables and equations are repositioned. The extensive token heatmaps are retained and renumbered from Figure 14 to Figure 12.

improvement.justification: Useful disclosures and some clearer wording are outweighed by losing the larger-model ablations and broader sensitivity evidence from v1 Appendix C.4–C.5. v2 also introduces an inconsistency between its 47% abstract claim and unchanged 36% conclusion. Revised scores alone establish no quality gain. The methodological core and broad benchmark coverage remain intact, so the overall decline is limited.
